stories.title: ‘A natural ability of getting someone to open up’: The therapy dogs helping ease exam season stress
stories.summary: Therapaws of Michigan, a volunteer organization with over 120 dog-human pairs, provides therapy dog visits to more than 25 locations in Washtenaw County, including the University of Michigan during exam season and local elementary schools, offering emotional support and comfort.

stories.title: Massive Google data center faces decision day in Michigan’s Van Buren Township
stories.summary: Van Buren Township is poised to approve a Google data center, with officials negotiating agreements to mitigate potential environmental impacts and utility cost increases for residents. The township supervisor indicated that Google will cover any residential water rate hikes and has reduced generator reliance, while tax incentives were used to secure advanced environmental controls and sound dampening measures.

inputFacts.title: Massive Google data center faces decision day in Michigan’s Van Buren Township
inputFacts.summary: The Van Buren Township Planning Commission is set to vote on the final site for a Google data center on October 14. Residents express concerns about environmental impact and utility costs, while Supervisor Kevin McNamara emphasizes the need to comply with zoning laws and negotiate community benefits. The township has secured agreements to mitigate potential issues like water rate increases and power outages.

stories.title: PCEP Peer to Peer Program Promotes Inclusive Environment
stories.summary: The Plymouth-Canton Community Schools' Peer to Peer Program at PCEP fosters an inclusive environment by pairing general education students with special education students for activities like learning, music, and social events. The program, which has a broad research base, aims to create meaningful connections and develop skills for all participants, with plans to expand into areas like team games and entrepreneurship.

inputFacts.title: PCEP Peer to Peer Program Promotes Inclusive Environment
inputFacts.summary: The Peer to Peer Program at Plymouth Canton Education Park (PCEP) fosters inclusive connections between students with and without disabilities through collaborative activities like quizzes, music sessions, and social events. Led by Jacklyn Klotz and special education teachers, the program is recognized as an Evidence-Based Practice for students with disabilities and aims to expand with new initiatives like team games and entrepreneurship training.

inputFacts.title: Woman accused of robbing 18-year-old at gunpoint at Plymouth Township gas station
inputFacts.summary: Diamond Dominique-Marie Jones, 35, was charged with armed robbery after allegedly stealing a wallet and phone from an 18-year-old at gunpoint at a Plymouth Township gas station on Oct. 11. Police arrested Jones at a Dearborn gas station, recovering the stolen items and a suspected gun. She was arraigned on Oct. 13 with a $50,000 bond and faces multiple charges including armed robbery and felony firearm.

inputFacts.title: Devin Scillian shares what life has been like after retiring on ‘Local Blend’ podcast
inputFacts.summary: Devin Scillian discusses his retirement from TV news, his playwriting projects, and reflections on his career during an interview on the ‘Local Blend’ podcast. He shares insights into writing his play 'Bastard' and the transition to retirement. The episode explores his return to theater and creative pursuits.

inputFacts.title: Children found safe in Ohio cornfield after being abducted from Inkster; father found dead at scene
inputFacts.summary: Two boys, ages 6 and 4, were found safe in a cornfield near Norwalk, Ohio, after being allegedly abducted by their father, Brandon Deandre Lee, 36, during a domestic violence incident in Inkster, Michigan. Lee was found dead at the scene after reportedly threatening to kill himself and the children. The mother sustained minor injuries and coordinated with police to locate the children, who were later returned to Michigan with assistance from multiple agencies.

inputFacts.title: Michigan residents invited to observe voting machine testing ahead of General Election
inputFacts.summary: Michigan residents are invited to observe voting machine testing ahead of the General Election. The event is organized by local authorities to ensure transparency in the electoral process. Observations will take place in Ann Arbor and Ypsilanti.

inputFacts.title: 54-year-old bicyclist killed after being hit by car in Canton Township
inputFacts.summary: A 54-year-old Superior Township man died after being struck by a car while riding his bicycle in Canton Township. The crash occurred at approximately 6:30 p.m. Tuesday, Oct. 13, near Ford Road and Southford Road. Police reported the driver was a 26-year-old Indiana woman in a gold Toyota Camry, and the man was pronounced dead at the hospital.

inputFacts.title: TheRide receives $6.6 million state grant for Bus Rapid Transit study
inputFacts.summary: The state of Michigan awarded the Ann Arbor Area Transportation Authority $6.6 million to study a potential Bus Rapid Transit route aimed at decreasing commuting times on Washtenaw Avenue, as announced by Gov. Gretchen Whitmer. The study will explore creating a BRT route following the Interstate 94 Business Loop.

inputFacts.title: Who is umichgreg? Meet the account romanticizing the U-M campus
inputFacts.summary: The @umichgreg TikTok account is romanticizing the University of Michigan campus with videos featuring scenes like West Hall under golden light and Taylor Swift’s music, offering students a moment to slow down and appreciate campus life.

inputFacts.title: Election Day is just ahead. How to vote now and beat the lines
inputFacts.summary: Michigan voters can cast ballots early via absentee or in-person voting ahead of the Nov. 3 election. Absentee ballots can be submitted by mail, in person, or via drop boxes, while early voting sites operate for a minimum of nine days ending the Sunday before the election. The gubernatorial race features Jocelyn Benson (D) vs. John James (R).

inputFacts.title: Groves High School celebrates inclusion with Victory Day event during Powderpuff football game
inputFacts.summary: Groves High School hosted a Victory Day event during its Powderpuff football game to provide students with disabilities an opportunity to shine on the field. The event was part of efforts to promote inclusion and celebrate diverse student abilities.

inputFacts.title: Student arrested for assaulting, hospitalizing teacher at Emerson Elementary-Middle School
inputFacts.summary: A student was arrested after assaulting and hospitalizing a special education teacher at Emerson Elementary-Middle School. The teacher has since been released and is recovering at home, while the student was expelled. Details about the incident's location or circumstances remain unclear.

inputFacts.title: From record heat to rainy, cool end of workweek in Metro Detroit
inputFacts.summary: Meteorologist Ron Hilliard reports a transition from record heat to rainy and cooler conditions by the end of the workweek in Metro Detroit. The weather update includes publication and update timestamps for October 14, 2026.

inputFacts.title: How much will diesel tax exemptions save you? Michigan tax rate
inputFacts.summary: Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer declared a state of energy emergency to suspend rules for farm and forestry vehicles, reducing diesel costs by 52.4 cents per gallon in addition to President Donald Trump's federal tax deferral. The combined measures aim to alleviate financial strain on agricultural producers and loggers during peak harvest season amid high fuel prices. Michigan's average diesel price is $6.48 per gallon, down from $6.89 in September but significantly higher than $3.65 a year ago.

inputFacts.title: Woman robs teen at gunpoint in Plymouth Twp. gas station, police say
inputFacts.summary: A woman suspected of robbing a customer at gunpoint at a Plymouth Township gas station was arrested after police located her in Dearborn. The 18-year-old victim reported a black semiautomatic pistol was used to steal her wallet and cellphone. Investigators believe the suspect may be connected to other serious crimes in metro Detroit.

inputFacts.title: Michigan regulators OK DTE contracts for Google data center
inputFacts.summary: Michigan regulators approved DTE Energy contracts to power Google’s 1-gigawatt data center in Van Buren Township, with conditions to protect existing utility customers. The Wayne County Commission also overrode a veto to grant Google a tax exemption. Critics and Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel raised concerns about potential stranded assets and grid reliability risks.
